title: Audio output is floor-truncated to 16 bits without dither, including on drivers that hand the OS float (WASAPI, Web)
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.1.stable [a13da4feb] (Linux, and a Web export), 4.7.stable [5b4e0cb0f] (macOS).
- The conversion code is the same in 4.7.2.stable [ed1daf0bf] and on master at [e7cfa294a] (read, not built).
- Not a regression: the same int32 packing and `>> 16` are in 3.0.stable and 4.0.stable (read, not run).

### System information

Measured on three systems, all with the official builds:  - **Linux:** Godot v4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb] - Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, x86_64 (headless container, no GPU, `--display-driver headless`) - audio driver: PulseAudio (server 16.1) - output device: null sink, float32le, 2 ch, 48000 Hz - mix rate 48000 Hz - **macOS:** Godot v4.7.stable.official [5b4e0cb0f] - macOS 15.7.9 (24G830) - MacBook Air (15-inch, M2), 8 GB (`--display-driver headless`) - audio driver: CoreAudio - output device: Pro Tools Audio Bridge 2-B (a virtual loopback device), float32, 2 ch, 48000 Hz - mix rate 48000 Hz - **Web:** export from Godot v4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb] with the official templates, thread support on - Chromium 141.0.7390.37, headless, on the Linux system above (software-rendered WebGL 2) - audio driver: AudioWorklet - AudioContext at 48000 Hz  Not measured: Windows (WASAPI, XAudio2), Android (OpenSL ES), Linux ALSA. Those are read from the source.

### Issue description

The mixer works in float. On the way to the device the signal is quantized twice, and neither step rounds or dithers.

1. `AudioServer::_driver_process()` clamps each sample, multiplies it by `(1 << 20) - 1`, truncates toward zero and shifts the magnitude left by 11. The result is a 21-bit value in an `int32_t`:
   https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/servers/audio/audio_server.cpp#L96-L105
2. Each output driver then keeps the top 16 bits with an arithmetic `>> 16`, which is floor (rounding toward −∞):
   - CoreAudio (macOS, iOS, visionOS), 16-bit signed-integer stream format: [L146-L151](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/drivers/coreaudio/audio_driver_coreaudio.mm#L146-L151), [L217](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/drivers/coreaudio/audio_driver_coreaudio.mm#L217)
   - PulseAudio, `PA_SAMPLE_S16LE`: [L234](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/drivers/pulseaudio/audio_driver_pulseaudio.cpp#L234), [L426](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/drivers/pulseaudio/audio_driver_pulseaudio.cpp#L426)
   - ALSA, `SND_PCM_FORMAT_S16_LE`: [L108](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/drivers/alsa/audio_driver_alsa.cpp#L108), [L218](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/drivers/alsa/audio_driver_alsa.cpp#L218)
   - OpenSL ES (Android), `SL_PCMSAMPLEFORMAT_FIXED_16`: [L135-L136](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/platform/android/audio_driver_opensl.cpp#L135-L136), [L70](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/platform/android/audio_driver_opensl.cpp#L70)
   - XAudio2 (not built by default): [L69-L70](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/drivers/xaudio2/audio_driver_xaudio2.cpp#L69-L70), [L101](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/drivers/xaudio2/audio_driver_xaudio2.cpp#L101)
   - WASAPI with a float mix format, `(sample >> 16) / 32768.f`: [L733](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/drivers/wasapi/audio_driver_wasapi.cpp#L733)
   - Web, `float(stream_buffer[i] >> 16) / 32768.f`: [L86](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/platform/web/audio_driver_web.cpp#L86), [L94](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/platform/web/audio_driver_web.cpp#L94)

WASAPI and Web hand the OS float32, but only after cutting it to the 16-bit grid. What they deliver is therefore identical to an undithered 16-bit word, even though nothing downstream needs 16 bits. (WASAPI's 24- and 32-bit PCM branches keep the 21 bits, but shared mode normally reports a float mix format.)

#### Measured

The attached project plays a 997 Hz sine from an `AudioStreamGenerator` on Master with no effects: 5 s at −6 dBFS, then 5 s at −100 dBFS. An `AudioEffectCapture` on Master writes the float frames the mixer hands to the driver to a file, which is the reference. I recorded the output bit for bit on three systems:

- **Linux, PulseAudio:** the float32 monitor of a null sink.
- **macOS, CoreAudio:** the input side of a virtual loopback device, read with a HAL IOProc. The loopback was first shown to return float noise that is off the 16-bit grid unchanged, bit for bit, so the grid in the recording is Godot's.
- **Web, AudioWorklet:** the samples Godot's audio node hands to `AudioContext.destination`, tapped inside the page.

The result is the same on all three, to the sample:

| Measure | Result |
|---|---|
| Output samples × 32768 | all integers: the output sits on the 16-bit grid, including the float handed to Web Audio |
| Output against the two steps above, applied to the reference | identical over the whole 10 s signal, 0 mismatches |
| THD+N at −6 dBFS, 20 Hz–20 kHz, float reference (before the driver) | −153.7 dB |
| THD+N at −6 dBFS, 20 Hz–20 kHz, output | −92.9 dB |
| DC offset of the output at −6 dBFS | −0.48 LSB |
| Output values across 4 s at −100 dBFS | 0 (101,836 samples) and −1 LSB (90,164 samples), never +1 |

WASAPI, ALSA, OpenSL ES and XAudio2 are read from the source at the lines linked above and not measured; I have no Windows machine to hand. `tools/measure.py` in the attached zip takes any bit-exact recording of the project's output and says whether it matches.

−92.9 dB is the expected figure for plain 16-bit quantization of a −6 dBFS sine in a 20 kHz band at 48 kHz. I am not asking for more than 16 bits here. I am reporting that the 16-bit conversion itself is done incorrectly:

- **Floor instead of round** puts a DC offset of about −½ LSB on the output.
- **No dither** makes the error correlated with the signal, so it is distortion rather than noise. It shows on fades, reverb tails and quiet passages, which is where it is audible.
- **Below 1 LSB the output is one-sided.** Positive samples below 2⁻¹⁵ become 0. Negative samples from 2⁻²⁰ (about −120 dBFS) up to 1 LSB in magnitude become −1 LSB. A sine at −100 dBFS therefore leaves the driver as −1 LSB pulses on its negative half-cycles only.

Expected: the conversion to a 16-bit sink rounds and uses TPDF dither (±1 LSB triangular), so the error is signal-independent noise with no DC. A sink that accepts float receives float that has not been cut to 16 bits.

Requested, within this issue:
1. **Round and apply TPDF dither where the output is a 16-bit integer.** One shared conversion helper in `AudioDriver`, called by the 16-bit drivers in place of `>> 16`, would cover CoreAudio, PulseAudio, ALSA, OpenSL ES and XAudio2. Dither applied unconditionally in `_driver_process()` would also add 16-bit-level noise to WASAPI's 24- and 32-bit PCM branches, which do not need it.
2. **Do not cut to the 16-bit grid on sinks that already take float** (WASAPI float mix format, Web). Pass the mixed float through, or at least convert from the full `int32_t` rather than from `sample >> 16`.

Related, but a feature request and so not part of this bug: a float or 24-bit output path on the drivers that are integer today (CoreAudio `kAudioFormatFlagIsFloat`, `PA_SAMPLE_FLOAT32LE`, ALSA `FLOAT_LE`, OpenSL ES `PCM_EX` float or AAudio). That is godotengine/godot-proposals#8797 (see also godotengine/godot-proposals#8815 and godotengine/godot-proposals#12908). Draft PR #90013 adds format-tagged buffers that would give WASAPI and Web true float. The PipeWire driver in #111056 currently uses `SPA_AUDIO_FORMAT_S16` with `>> 16` as well.

### Steps to reproduce

Unzip the attached project. Each recipe records what the device receives, then compares it with the reference the project writes. `measure.py` needs numpy.

**Linux, PulseAudio**

```
pactl load-module module-null-sink sink_name=cap rate=48000 format=float32le channels=2
pactl set-default-sink cap
parec -d cap.monitor --format=float32le --rate=48000 --channels=2 --raw > device_f32le.raw &
godot --path sixteen_bit_floor_mrp --audio-driver PulseAudio
kill %1
python3 sixteen_bit_floor_mrp/tools/measure.py ~/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/"Sixteen-bit floor MRP"/reference_f32le.raw device_f32le.raw
```

On a machine with no display, add `--display-driver headless` (not `--headless`, which selects the Dummy audio driver).

**macOS, CoreAudio**, with any loopback device that carries 32-bit float (the terminal needs microphone permission to read its input):

```
cc -O2 -o halloop sixteen_bit_floor_mrp/tools/halloop.c -framework CoreAudio -framework CoreFoundation
./halloop selftest "Pro Tools Audio Bridge 2-B"      # must report: the loopback is bit-transparent
godot --path sixteen_bit_floor_mrp -- --output-device="?"   # prints the device names as Godot lists them
./halloop rec "Pro Tools Audio Bridge 2-B" 20 device_f32le.raw &
godot --path sixteen_bit_floor_mrp --display-driver headless --audio-driver CoreAudio -- --output-device="Pro Tools Audio Bridge 2-B (61)"
wait
python3 sixteen_bit_floor_mrp/tools/measure.py ~/Library/Application\ Support/Godot/app_userdata/"Sixteen-bit floor MRP"/reference_f32le.raw device_f32le.raw
```

**Web** (needs the export templates, Node, and `npm install playwright`):

```
mkdir web_threads
godot --headless --path sixteen_bit_floor_mrp --export-release "Web threads"
python3 sixteen_bit_floor_mrp/tools/serve.py web_threads 8062 &
node sixteen_bit_floor_mrp/tools/web_tap.mjs http://127.0.0.1:8062/index.html out
python3 sixteen_bit_floor_mrp/tools/measure.py out/reference_f32le.raw out/device_f32le.raw
```

The single-threaded preset (`"Web"`, into a folder named `web`) gives the same result. In headless Chromium with software rendering it cannot feed the worklet in real time, and `measure.py` skips the resulting blocks of silence (860 of them in my run).

**Windows, WASAPI:** not run. Any bit-exact loopback of the output at 48 kHz, saved as interleaved stereo float32, can be given to `measure.py`.

**Result**, the same five lines on all three systems (the frame counts on the first line vary):

```
device samples x 32768 are all integers: True
device vs model over 479999 of 479999 signal frames x 2 channels: 0 mismatches
-6 dBFS section, THD+N 20 Hz-20 kHz: reference -153.7 dB, device -92.9 dB
-6 dBFS section, device DC offset: -0.484 LSB
-100 dBFS section, 192000 frames, device values in LSB: {-1: 90164, 0: 101836}, mean -0.470
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Attached: one scene and one script, `project.godot` with the mix rate at 48000 (and `mix_rate.web` at 48000, so the Web export runs at the same rate), and two Web export presets. The `tools/` folder is ignored by the editor (`.gdignore`) and holds what the steps above use: `measure.py`, `halloop.c` (macOS loopback recorder), `web_tap.mjs` and `serve.py`.

The script takes one optional argument after `--`: `--output-device=NAME` plays to that device instead of the default, and quits without playing if it is absent. On Web the reference is offered as a download when the run ends.

[TG-0814_sixteen_bit_floor_mrp_2026-10-02.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32975401/TG-0814_sixteen_bit_floor_mrp_2026-10-02.zip)
